summary: Octagonal brownstone light at the New Haven Harbor entrance; first tower 1805, present tower 1845 or 1847, decommissioned 1877 when Southwest Ledge took over.

structures.note: Octagonal brownstone tower with brick lining. NRHP: placed in service 1845, about 80 ft. LighthouseFriends: completed 1847, 65 ft. USLHS place record: 70 ft.
First tower, octagonal wood, 30 ft, eight lamps in 13-inch reflectors (LighthouseFriends).

Keeper's dwelling about 30 ft east of the tower. NRHP dates it to the War of 1812; LighthouseFriends dates a two-and-a-half-storey dwelling to 1835. Private residence for city recreation staff in 1990.

access.note: Grounds open; dwelling and tower closed (LighthouseFriends). Tours through the East Shore Ranger Station.

facts.agency: City of New Haven (Lighthouse Point Park)

events.note: Jonathan Finch appointed first keeper on 19 December 1804
First lighthouse completed by the government
Brick keeper's dwelling built during the War of 1812 (NRHP c.1812)
Two-and-a-half-storey keeper's dwelling added (LighthouseFriends); conflicts with the NRHP's 1812 date
New brownstone tower placed in service (NRHP). LighthouseFriends gives completion in 1847 at $10,000 by Marcus Bassett.
Fourth-order Fresnel lens replaced the lamp system
Fog bell rung by a caloric engine

Repairs and renovation after the 15 July 1870 appropriation; a striking apparatus replaced the caloric engine (LighthouseFriends). The cast-iron lantern was probably installed in the late 1860s or early 1870s (NRHP).
Decommissioned when the Southwest Ledge light went into service on 1 January 1877
Transferred to the War Department on 13 November 1896 (Light-House Board report for fiscal 1897)
War Department lease ended; land to the State of Connecticut and buildings to the City of New Haven (LighthouseFriends)
City acquired the property for Lighthouse Point Park (NRHP). Conflicts with LighthouseFriends' 1922 date for the handover.
Lighthouse Point Park opened to the public (LighthouseFriends)
Tower renovated; interior steam cleaned and repainted (LighthouseFriends)
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places (NRIS 90001108)

keepers.name: Elizur Thompson
keepers.note: Left in 1867 for Alaskan gold and returned in 1869 with no money (LighthouseFriends). Kept the Southwest Ledge light until 1881, then custodian of Five Mile Point at one dollar a year until his death in 1898 (LighthouseFriends).

notes_for_editor: (1) Date of the present tower: 1845 'placed in service' and 'lighthouse completed' in the NRHP nomination (significant dates 1845), 1847 completion in LighthouseFriends; the station record carries both (USLHS 1845, Rowlett 1847). No Board report for 1845-1847 is in the local corpus (the corpus covers Board reports 1891-1901 only), so this is not resolved. (2) Heights: tower about 80 ft (NRHP) vs 65 ft (LighthouseFriends) vs 70 ft (USLHS place record, to lantern); focal plane 97 ft (LighthouseFriends) vs 93 ft (USLHS). (3) The keeper's dwelling: NRHP says a brick house built in the War of 1812; LighthouseFriends says a two-and-a-half-story dwelling was added in 1835 and places it just north of the tower, while the NRHP puts it about 30 ft east. (4) The 1922/1924 city-acquisition dates differ (LighthouseFriends: buildings to the city at lease end in 1922; NRHP: city acquired the property 1924). (5) Wikipedia's keeper list (which this research did not rely on) names Amos Morris Jr. as first keeper for three weeks, lists 'Wedmore' in 1805, and spells two keepers 'William Finch' and 'Merritt Thompson'; the USLHS roster and LighthouseFriends agree on Jonathan Finch from 1804 and on 'Milton Finch' and 'Merit Thompson'. (6) The 1806 advertisement and the 1868 Board report are known here only as quoted by LighthouseFriends; the originals were not read. (7) Chronicling America returned no Connecticut lighthouse pages for Five Mile Point from 1804-1880 and 11 general New Haven pages from 1877-1925 that did not describe this light; none was used. (8) No storms, wrecks or rescues at this light were found in the sources read, so that chapter is omitted. (9) The 1904 Life-Saving Service mention of a 'Five Mile Point, 17 miles ENE' concerns a different place and was not used. (10) LighthouseFriends is all rights reserved: facts are paraphrased; quotations in the evidence list are for checking only. (11) Elizur Thompson's Southwest Ledge service follows LighthouseFriends (until 1881); Wikipedia gives five years, not used. (12) Current access rests on LighthouseFriends' statement that the grounds are open and the dwelling and tower closed; the NRHP describes 1990 conditions only. (13) Sex of Sarah A. Bradley: neither the roster nor LighthouseFriends states it, so the story does not call her a woman; the roster gives her role as first assistant. (14) LighthouseFriends places the 1835 dwelling just north of the tower but its own text also says two-story in one place and two-and-a-half-story in another; the story gives the two-and-a-half-story figure from its keeper notes. (15) The 1806 advertisement and the 1868 Board report are quoted from LighthouseFriends; the originals were not read. (16) Southwest Ledge: the 'from 1877' start in the other_stations entry is inferred from the 1877 changeover; LighthouseFriends gives only the end year (1881).
